#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/orch/contract.sh — Orchestrator backend contract layer (ADR-011, issue #219)
#
# Defines the orchestrator backend interface contract.  Strategy plugins
# (issues #198/#199/#200) source this file and provide implementations of
# the five contract functions.  The contract layer itself provides:
#
#   orch_has_capability <cap>   — queries the loaded backend's capabilities
#   orch_load_backend   <alias> — finds and sources a backend plugin by alias
#
# On file load, _orch_load_backend is called automatically to wire up the
# configured backend.  If no plugin is found, no-op stubs remain in place so
# callers can detect the "not implemented" state gracefully.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail here.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ORCH_CONTRACT_LOADED=1

# Sentinel: 0 = only stubs loaded, 1 = a real backend plugin was sourced.
# If any contract function is already defined when this file is sourced, a
# backend was pre-loaded (sourced before this contract file).  Mark it loaded
# so _orch_load_backend does not overwrite those implementations.
if declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
   declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
else
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=0
fi

_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"

# ─── Scratch directory for pool state ───────────────────────────────────────
# #898: the default is computed at use-time in `_strategy_orch_scratch_dir`
# (core/pipeline/strategies/common.sh) so it can be re-rooted under the per-run
# state dir (~/.zbuild/state/runs/<run_id>/orch) once ZBUILD_RUN_ID is known —
# the orchestrator analog of #887/#889. An explicit ZBUILD_ORCH_SCRATCH still
# overrides. (Was: a flat ~/.zbuild/state/orch baked here at source time, before
# run_id existed, which made per-run isolation impossible.)

# ─── _orch_not_implemented ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Emits an event and returns 1. Used by contract stubs before a backend loads.
_orch_not_implemented() {
    local fn_name="$1"
    local context="${2:-(no pool)}"
    # Emit event if emit_event is available (event-bus may not be loaded yet)
    if declare -F emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        emit_event "orch.contract.not_implemented" "fn=${fn_name}" "context=${context}" || true
    fi
    warn "orch contract: ${fn_name} not implemented (context: ${context})" || true
    return 1
}

# ─── Contract stubs — overridden by backend source ──────────────────────────
# These are only defined if the backend has not already provided them.

if ! declare -F orch_spawn >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_spawn()        { _orch_not_implemented "orch_spawn" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_dispatch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_dispatch()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_dispatch" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_collect >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Exit code convention: 0 = all passed; 1 otherwise, with
    # _ORCH_COLLECT_OUTCOME = partial (some passed) | failed (#1850, ADR-054 §4:
    # partial was rc 2). Backends normalise work-unit exit codes — any non-zero
    # counts as fail; the original work-unit rc is NOT passed through.
    orch_collect()      { _orch_not_implemented "orch_collect" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_shutdown >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_shutdown()     { _orch_not_implemented "orch_shutdown" "$1"; }
fi

if ! declare -F orch_capabilities >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    orch_capabilities() { _orch_not_implemented "orch_capabilities" "(no pool)"; }
fi

# ─── orch_has_capability ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Queries the loaded backend's capability list.
# Usage: orch_has_capability <capability_name>
# Returns 0 if the capability is present in orch_capabilities output, 1 if not.
orch_has_capability() {
    local cap="$1"
    local caps
    caps="$(orch_capabilities 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if grep -qF "\"${cap}\"" <<< "$caps"; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_find_backend_dir ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lightweight backend plugin discovery that does NOT require the full registry.
# Scans $plugins_root for a plugin whose manifest declares:
#   provides.role: orchestrator-backend
#   AND (id: <alias> OR provides.alias: <alias>)
# Prints the plugin directory on success.  Returns 1 if not found.
_orch_find_backend_dir() {
    local alias="$1"
    local plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins}}"

    [[ -d "$plugins_root" ]] || return 1

    local manifest plugin_dir
    while IFS= read -r manifest; do
        plugin_dir="$(dirname "$manifest")"
        # Check provides.role
        if ! grep -q 'role:.*orchestrator-backend' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null; then
            continue
        fi
        # Check id or provides.alias match
        local id declared_alias
        id="$(awk '/^id:/ { sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        declared_alias="$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*alias:/ { sub(/^[[:space:]]*alias:[[:space:]]*/, ""); print; exit }' "$manifest" 2>/dev/null)"
        if [[ "$id" == "$alias" || "$declared_alias" == "$alias" ]]; then
            echo "$plugin_dir"
            return 0
        fi
    done < <(find "$plugins_root" -maxdepth 4 -name 'manifest.yaml' -type f 2>/dev/null)

    return 1
}

# ─── orch_load_backend ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Finds and sources a backend plugin by its alias.
# Usage: orch_load_backend <alias>
# Uses find_plugin_for_role (if available) or lightweight _orch_find_backend_dir
# to locate the plugin, then sources plugin.sh.
# No fallback: a missing or unreadable backend is a hard misconfigured error.
orch_load_backend() {
    local backend="${1:-}"
    local plugin_dir

    if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
        warn "orch_load_backend: no backend alias provided" || true
        return 1
    fi

    # Try registry lookup if find_plugin_for_role is available
    if declare -F find_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        plugin_dir="$(find_plugin_for_role "orchestrator-backend" "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
        if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
                warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
                _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
                return 1
            fi
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
            return 0
        fi
    fi

    # Fallback: lightweight scan without the full registry
    plugin_dir="$(_orch_find_backend_dir "$backend" 2>/dev/null)" || plugin_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$plugin_dir" && -f "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "${plugin_dir}/plugin.sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # Last-resort: try the built-in bash-parallel backend by its known repo path (#1801).
    # This resolves the default even when ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT does not include the
    # installed orch backends (common in integration tests that override ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT).
    # Only bash-parallel gets this treatment — it is the declared system default; any other
    # backend that reaches this point is truly misconfigured.
    local _bash_parallel_sh="${_ZBUILD_ROOT}/plugins/tool/orch-bash-parallel/plugin.sh"
    if [[ "$backend" == "bash-parallel" && -f "$_bash_parallel_sh" ]]; then
        if [[ ! -r "$_bash_parallel_sh" ]]; then
            warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' plugin.sh is not readable — misconfigured" || true
            _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
            return 1
        fi
        # shellcheck disable=SC1090
        source "$_bash_parallel_sh"
        _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED=1
        return 0
    fi

    # No plugin found — hard misconfigured error naming the backend.
    warn "orch_load_backend: backend '${backend}' not found — misconfigured (no plugin for role orchestrator-backend with alias '${backend}')" || true
    _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured
    return 1
}

# ─── _orch_load_backend (internal) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Called at end of file to auto-load the configured backend.
# Skips auto-loading if a backend has already provided the contract functions
# (i.e., when a plugin sources the backend before sourcing this contract file).
_orch_load_backend() {
    # If a real backend was already sourced (sentinel set to 1), skip auto-load
    # to avoid overwriting the pre-loaded backend's implementations.
    # Note: the stubs above do NOT set this sentinel, so checking declare -F
    # would always return true (stubs are defined).  We use the sentinel instead.
    [[ "${_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED:-0}" -eq 1 ]] && return 0

    local backend

    # Get configured backend; default is bash-parallel (the system default, #1801).
    # "sequential" is no longer a valid backend alias — any unknown alias fails misconfigured.
    if declare -F zbuild_config_get_backend >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        backend="$(zbuild_config_get_backend "orchestrator" 2>/dev/null)" || backend="bash-parallel"
    else
        backend="${ZBUILD_ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND:-bash-parallel}"
    fi

    # Attempt to load the configured backend; if it fails, that is OK —
    # the stubs remain and callers will get informative errors.
    orch_load_backend "$backend" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# Auto-load at source time — skipped if _ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_LOADED is already 1
_orch_load_backend

content.thinking:
Good. The contract.sh looks like it has been updated to remove the sequential fallback and replace with bash-parallel. But there's a big issue - the `_orch_load_backend` function uses `|| true` on the `orch_load_backend` call, meaning if the backend load fails (misconfigured), it silently swallows the error. This means when the backend is missing, the stubs remain and callers get stub errors instead of proper misconfigured results.

But wait, the SPEC-2/4/10 tests need it to fail as `misconfigured` *naming the backend*. The runner needs to detect that `_ZBUILD_ORCH_BACKEND_DISPOSITION=misconfigured` after `_orch_load_backend` and fail the run.
Let me check how the runner itself handles that misconfigured disposition.

121	                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
122	  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
123	  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
124	  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
125	  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
126	  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
127	  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
128	  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no

156	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
157	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
158	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
159	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
160	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
161	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
162	_runner_retry_budget() {
163	    local v=""
164	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
165	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
166	    fi
167	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
168	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
169	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
170	    printf '%s' "$v"
171	}

173	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
174	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
175	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
176	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
177	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
178	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
179	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
180	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
181	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
182	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
183	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
184	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
185	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
186	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
187	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
188	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
189	    _runner_ended=true
190	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
191	    return 0
192	}
193	
194	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
195	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
196	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
197	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
198	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
199	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
200	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
201	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
202	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
203	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
204	    case "$v" in
205	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
206	        *) return 1 ;;
207	    esac
208	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
209	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
210	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
211	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
212	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
213	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
214	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
215	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
216	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
217	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
218	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
219	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
220	    _runner_ended=true
221	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
222	    return 0
223	}

225	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
226	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
227	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
228	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
229	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
230	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
231	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
232	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
233	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
234	    local latest="" n=0 d k
235	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
236	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
237	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
238	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
239	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
240	    done
241	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
242	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
243	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
244	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
245	        return
246	    fi
247	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
248	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
249	}

251	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
252	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
253	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
254	_runner_note_push_failure() {
255	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
256	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
257	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
258	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
259	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
260	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
261	}

263	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
264	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
265	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
266	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
267	# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
268	# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
269	# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
270	# reported, never fatal.
271	_runner_push_work_branch() {
272	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
273	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
274	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
275	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
276	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
277	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
278	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
279	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
280	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
281	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
282	    local _err
283	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
284	        return 0
285	    fi
286	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
287	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
288	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
289	    return 0
290	}

292	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
293	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
294	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
295	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
296	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
297	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
298	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
299	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
300	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
301	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
302	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
303	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
304	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
305	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
306	        reattached)
307	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
308	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
309	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
310	        diverged)
311	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
312	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
313	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
314	    esac
315	    return 0
316	}

318	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
319	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
320	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
321	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
322	# never blocks a run.
323	#
324	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
325	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
326	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
327	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
328	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
329	# item 1 of #1807.
330	#
331	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
332	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
333	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
334	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
335	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
336	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
337	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
338	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
339	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
340	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
341	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
342	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
343	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
344	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
345	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
346	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
347	    # push had nothing to send.
348	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
349	
350	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
351	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
352	        saved)
353	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
354	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
355	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
356	            ;;
357	        failed)
358	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
359	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
360	            # no channel to surface on.
361	            #
362	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
363	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
364	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
365	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
366	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
367	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
368	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
369	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
370	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
371	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
372	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
373	            fi
374	            ;;
375	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
376	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
377	        *) : ;;
378	    esac
379	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
380	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
381	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
382	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
383	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
384	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
385	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
386	    local _leak=""
387	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
388	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
389	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"

493	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
494	_runner_now_short() {
495	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"

510	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
511	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
512	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
513	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
514	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
515	_runner_duration_token() {
516	    local stage="$1"
517	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
518	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
519	        printf '?s'
520	        return 0
521	    fi
522	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
523	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
524	        printf '?s'
525	        return 0
526	    fi
527	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
528	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
529	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
530	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
531	    else
532	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
533	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
534	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
535	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
536	    fi
537	}

573	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
574	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
575	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
576	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
577	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
578	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
579	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
580	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
581	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
582	_runner_record_report() {
583	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
584	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
585	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
586	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
587	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
588	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
589	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
590	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
591	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
592	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
593	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
594	        sleep 0.05
595	    done
596	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
597	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
598	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
599	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
600	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
601	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
602	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
603	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
604	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
605	    else
606	        rm -f "$tmp"
607	    fi
608	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
609	    return 0
610	}

612	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
613	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
614	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
615	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
616	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
617	#
618	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
619	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
620	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
621	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
622	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
623	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
624	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
625	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
626	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
627	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
628	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
629	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
630	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
631	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
632	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
633	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
634	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
635	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
636	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
637	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
638	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
639	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
640	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
641	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
642	        return 1
643	    fi
644	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
645	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
646	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
647	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
648	        return 1
649	    fi
650	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
651	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
652	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
653	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
654	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
655	    #
656	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
657	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
658	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
659	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
660	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
661	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
662	    #
663	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
664	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
665	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
666	    #
667	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
668	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
669	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
670	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
671	    fi
672	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
673	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
674	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
675	    # an unchanged tree.
676	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
677	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
678	    fi
679	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
680	    local _leaf _ok=1
681	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
682	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
683	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
684	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
685	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
686	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
687	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
688	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
689	        esac
690	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
691	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
692	            _ok=0
693	        fi
694	    done
695	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
696	}

698	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
699	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
700	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
701	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
702	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
703	#
704	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
705	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
706	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
707	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
708	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
709	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
710	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
711	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
712	#
713	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
714	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
715	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
716	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
717	#
718	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
719	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
720	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
721	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
722	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
723	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
724	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
725	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
726	_runner_template_personas() {
727	    awk '
728	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
729	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
730	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
731	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
732	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
733	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
734	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
735	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
736	        }
737	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
738	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
739	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
740	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
741	        }
742	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
743	}

745	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
746	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
747	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
748	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
749	    case "$mode" in
750	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
751	        *) mode="warn" ;;
752	    esac
753	
754	    # off = complete no-op, no output
755	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
756	
757	    local -a violations=()
758	    local fail_count=0
759	
760	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
761	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
762	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")

766	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
767	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
768	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
769	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
770	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
771	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
772	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
773	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
774	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
775	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
776	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
777	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
778	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
779	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
780	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")

788	    # pre-dispatch input presence check reuses it instead of being a third
789	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
790	    _inputs_render_violations \
791	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
792	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
793	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
794	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
795	        "${violations[@]}"

798	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
800	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
801	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
802	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true
803	    fi
804	
805	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
806	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
807	        return 0
808	    fi
809	
810	    # enforce: fail-closed
811	    return 1
812	}
813	
814	# _runner_resume_intent <no_resume:true|false> — 1 (resume: reuse prior work)
815	# or 0 (recreate). The default is to resume (#2225); --no-resume, or
816	# ZBUILD_RESUME=0 already in the environment, recreates.
817	_runner_resume_intent() {
818	    if [[ "${1:-false}" == "true" || "${ZBUILD_RESUME:-1}" == "0" ]]; then
819	        printf '0'
820	    else
821	        printf '1'
822	    fi
823	}
824	
825	# _runner_startup_preflight_gate <dry_run> <resume_mode> (ADR-051 §warn-first, #1318)
826	# Testable gateway: calls _runner_validate_startup_preflight only when neither
827	# --dry-run nor --resume is active, matching the leaf_resolvability exemption.
828	# Extracted so the call-site condition is independently unit-testable (SPEC-5).
829	_runner_startup_preflight_gate() {
830	    local dry_run="${1:-false}" resume_mode="${2:-false}"
831	    if ! $dry_run && ! $resume_mode; then
832	        _runner_validate_startup_preflight || return $?
833	    fi
834	    return 0
835	}
836	
837	# ─── _runner_pipeline_duration_token (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
838	# Parallel to _runner_duration_token but for the pipeline-wide window. No stage
839	# argument — reads _RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS directly. Returns "?s" on cache
840	# miss so the banner still renders during very-early failures.
841	_runner_pipeline_duration_token() {
842	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"
843	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
844	        printf '?s'
845	        return 0
846	    fi
847	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
848	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
849	        printf '?s'
850	        return 0
851	    fi
852	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
853	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
854	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
855	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
856	    else
857	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
858	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
859	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
860	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
861	    fi
862	}
863	
864	# ─── _pipeline_status_glyph <status> (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
865	# Thin shim mapping the ADR-006 pipeline status enum to a verdict class glyph
866	# (delegates to verdict_glyph from core/pipeline/verdict.sh, #507). The
867	# pipeline status enum is distinct from plugin verdicts on purpose — this is
868	# a render-only mapping for the terminal banner, NOT an extension of the
869	# verdict table itself.
870	#
871	# Mapping:
872	#   complete (banner-only; persisted event payload still says "success")
873	#                                          → pass  → ✓
874	#   failed | interrupted | aborted         → fail  → ✗
875	#   preflight_failed                       → warn  → ⚠
876	#   anything else                          → ⚠ (defensive)
877	_pipeline_status_glyph() {
878	    local status="${1:-}"
879	    case "$status" in
880	        complete|success)              verdict_glyph "pass" ;;
881	        complete_unconverged)          verdict_glyph "warn" ;;
882	        failed|interrupted|aborted)    verdict_glyph "fail" ;;
883	        preflight_failed)              verdict_glyph "warn" ;;
884	        *)                             printf '%s' "?" ;;
885	    esac
886	}
887	
888	# ─── _pipeline_status_color <status> (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
889	# Companion to _pipeline_status_glyph; delegates to verdict_color so NO_COLOR
890	# behavior matches the per-stage indicator line exactly.
891	_pipeline_status_color() {
892	    local status="${1:-}"
893	    case "$status" in
894	        complete|success)              verdict_color "pass" ;;
895	        complete_unconverged)          verdict_color "warn" ;;
896	        failed|interrupted|aborted)    verdict_color "fail" ;;
897	        preflight_failed)              verdict_color "warn" ;;
898	        *)                             printf '%s' "${YELLOW:-}" ;;
899	    esac
900	}
901	
902	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
903	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
904	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
905	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
906	#
907	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
908	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
909	#
910	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
911	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
912	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
913	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
914	#
915	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
916	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
917	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
918	# against banner-write failures.
919	# _runner_restore_stderr — point fd 2 back at the runner's own stderr, saved at
920	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made
921	# with 2>/dev/null runs under that redirect, so the abort banner went to
922	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.
923	_runner_restore_stderr() {
924	    [[ -n "${_RUNNER_ERR_FD:-}" ]] && exec 2>&"$_RUNNER_ERR_FD"
925	    return 0
926	}
927	
928	_render_pipeline_end() {
929	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
930	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
931	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
932	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
933	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
934	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
935	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
936	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
937	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
938	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
939	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
940	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
941	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
942	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
943	    # (#1156)
944	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
945	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
946	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
947	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
948	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
949	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
950	
951	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
952	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
953	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
954	    local word
955	    case "$status" in
956	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
957	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
958	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
959	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
960	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
961	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
962	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
963	    esac
964	
965	    local label=" pipeline.end "
966	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
967	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
968	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
969	
970	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
971	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
972	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
973	
974	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
975	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
976	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
977	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
978	        local bar
979	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
980	        bar="${bar// /═}"
981	        {
982	            printf '\n'
983	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
984	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
985	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
986	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
987	        } >&2
988	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
989	        return 0
990	    fi
991	
992	    local lbar rbar
993	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
994	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
995	    {
996	        printf '\n'
997	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
998	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
999	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1000	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
1001	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
1002	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
1003	    } >&2
1004	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
1005	}
1006	
1007	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
1008	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
1009	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
1010	_runner_render_open_items() {
1011	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
1012	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1013	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n
1014	    items="$(open_items_markdown "$sd")" || items=""
1015	    n=0; [[ -n "$items" ]] && n="$(grep -c '^[0-9][0-9]*\. ' <<< "$items" || true)"
1016	    {
1017	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}" "$n")"
1018	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1019	    } >&2
1020	}
1021	
1022	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1023	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1024	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1025	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1026	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1027	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1028	#
1029	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1030	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1031	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1032	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1033	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1034	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1035	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1036	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1037	_render_stage_divider() {
1038	    local stage="$1"
1039	    local width
1040	    width="$(_term_width)"
1041	    local color
1042	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1043	    local label=" ${stage} "
1044	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1045	
1046	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1047	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1048	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1049	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1050	
1051	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1052	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1053	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1054	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1055	        local bar
1056	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1057	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1058	        {
1059	            printf '\n'
1060	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1061	            printf '\n'
1062	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1063	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1064	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1065	            printf '\n'
1066	        } >&2
1067	        return 0
1068	    fi
1069	
1070	    local lbar rbar
1071	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1072	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1073	    {
1074	        printf '\n'
1075	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1076	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1077	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1078	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1079	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1080	        printf '\n'
1081	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1082	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1083	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1084	        printf '\n'
1085	    } >&2
1086	}
1087	
1088	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1089	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1090	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1091	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1092	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1093	#
1094	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1095	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1096	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1097	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1098	#
1099	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1100	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1101	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1102	#     banner=best-effort).
1103	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1104	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1105	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1106	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1107	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1108	#
1109	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1110	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1111	
1112	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1113	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1114	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1115	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1116	_render_cycle_entry() {
1117	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1118	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1119	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1120	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1121	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1122	    local bar
1123	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1124	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1125	    {
1126	        printf '\n'
1127	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1128	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1129	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1130	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1131	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1132	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1133	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1134	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1135	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1136	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1137	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1138	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1139	        fi
1140	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1141	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1142	        printf '\n'
1143	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1144	}
1145	
1146	# ─── _render_parallel_entry <group_id> <max_parallel> <members_csv> ──────────
1147	# ADR-039 (#1131): clone of _render_cycle_entry for a parallel stage group.
1148	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering parallel group <id>` line + DIM
1149	# trailer (max_parallel + members). Emitted by the runner BEFORE
1150	# parallel_group_run so the operator's eye finds the group boundary first.
1151	_render_parallel_entry() {
1152	    local group_id="$1" max="$2" members_csv="${3:-}"
1153	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1154	    local label=" parallel: ${group_id} "
1155	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1156	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1157	    local bar
1158	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1159	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1160	    {
1161	        printf '\n'
1162	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1163	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1164	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1165	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1166	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1167	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1168	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1169	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1170	        printf '\n'
1171	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1172	}
1173	
1174	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1175	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1176	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1177	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1178	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1179	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1180	    {
1181	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1182	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1183	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1184	}
1185	
1186	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1187	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1188	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1189	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1190	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1191	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1192	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1193	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1194	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1195	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1196	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1197	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1198	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1199	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1200	    local label
1201	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1202	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1203	    else
1204	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1205	    fi
1206	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1207	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1208	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1209	    local bar
1210	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1211	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1212	    {
1213	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1214	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1215	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1216	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1217	}
1218	
1219	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1220	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1221	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1222	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1223	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1224	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1225	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1226	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1227	    {
1228	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1229	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1230	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/runner.sh — Pipeline orchestrator (issue #83, #208, #222, #225)
# ADR-001 (plugin contract), ADR-006 (resume contract), ADR-009 (platform-aware modularity),

_usage() {
    # Usage shown on error or --help. Unix convention: stderr (#619).
    cat >&2 <<EOF
Usage: runner.sh --issue <N>|--goal "<text>" [--dry-run] [--template <id>]
                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no
                    prior-run work (default: resume, reusing prior work;
                    ZBUILD_RESUME=0 is the same, #2225)
  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)

Environment:
  ZBUILD_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE  Force a single platform; detection short-circuits.
  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).
  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR   Override dir contract-reader stages source grammar libs from.
EOF
}

# Helpers extracted to dispatch.sh / state_helpers.sh in #279:
#   _find_plugin_for_stage       → core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
